items.q: I ______ this novel since Monday, and I still haven't reached the last chapter.
items.vi: Tôi đọc cuốn tiểu thuyết này từ thứ Hai mà vẫn chưa tới chương cuối.
items.explanation: An action that began in the past (since Monday) and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous: have been reading. The present simple, past simple and past continuous cannot go with since + a starting point.

items.q: Lan: How much is the bus ______ to the cinema? / Nam: Only seven thousand dong each way.
items.vi: Lan: Vé xe buýt tới rạp chiếu phim bao nhiêu tiền? / Nam: Chỉ bảy nghìn đồng một chiều thôi.
items.explanation: The money you pay for a bus, taxi or train ride is a fare. A fee is paid for a service (a doctor, a school), a price is for goods in a shop, and a charge is a general amount a company asks for, not the fixed word for transport.

items.q: My parents ______ for my sister's wedding party: a live band, fireworks and a five-tier cake.
items.vi: Bố mẹ tôi đã dốc toàn lực cho tiệc cưới của chị tôi: ban nhạc sống, pháo hoa và chiếc bánh cưới năm tầng.
items.explanation: Pull out all the stops means to make every possible effort so that something is a success. Pull strings is to use influence, pull your socks up is to start working harder, and pull someone's leg is to joke with them.

items.q: My brother ______ the housework on Saturdays while I cook lunch.
items.vi: Anh tôi làm việc nhà vào thứ Bảy còn tôi nấu bữa trưa.
items.explanation: We do the housework, the shopping and the washing-up; make goes with things you create (make a cake, make a decision). Take and give do not collocate with housework.

items.q: That's the singer ______ concert we went to last month.
items.vi: Đó là ca sĩ mà tháng trước chúng tôi đã đi xem buổi hòa nhạc của cô ấy.
items.explanation: The concert belongs to the singer, so we need the possessive relative whose + noun. Who and whom replace a person, not a possession, and which is for things.

items.q: Minh's birthday party has been ______ until next Saturday because his mother is ill.
items.vi: Tiệc sinh nhật của Minh đã bị hoãn đến thứ Bảy tuần sau vì mẹ cậu ấy bị ốm.
items.explanation: Put off means to postpone, which fits until next Saturday. Put out is to extinguish a fire, put up is to build or to give someone a bed, and set off is to start a journey.

items.q: To save money, my friends and I stayed at a cheap ______ where we shared a room with six other travellers.
items.vi: Để tiết kiệm tiền, tôi và bạn bè ở một nhà nghỉ tập thể giá rẻ, chung phòng với sáu du khách khác.
items.explanation: A hostel is cheap accommodation where travellers share large rooms. In a hotel or resort you have your own room, and at a campsite you sleep in a tent, not in a room.

items.q: Nam ______ the film last night — he was at my house until midnight.
items.vi: Nam không thể nào đã xem bộ phim tối qua được — cậu ấy ở nhà tôi đến tận nửa đêm.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle says something was impossible in the past: he was with me, so seeing the film was impossible. Must have expresses near certainty that it happened, might have a possibility, and should have an action that was expected but not done.

items.q: There were only ______ guests at the party, so we all sat around one table.
items.vi: Bữa tiệc chỉ có vài vị khách, nên tất cả chúng tôi ngồi quanh một bàn.
items.explanation: Guests is a countable plural, so it takes few / a few, not little / a little. After only we use a few (a small number); few on its own means almost none and does not follow only.

items.q: By the time we found our seats, the film ______.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi tìm được chỗ ngồi thì bộ phim đã bắt đầu rồi.
items.explanation: By the time + past simple (found) needs the past perfect for the earlier action: had already started. Present forms cannot combine with a past-time clause.

items.q: After the doctor's visit, my father decided ______ smoking for good.
items.vi: Sau khi đi khám bác sĩ, bố tôi quyết định bỏ hẳn thuốc lá.
items.explanation: Decide is followed by a to-infinitive: decided to give up. The gerund and the bare infinitive do not follow decide, and to giving up is not a form that exists after this verb.

items.q: From our hotel balcony we had a wonderful ______ of the harbour.
items.vi: Từ ban công khách sạn, chúng tôi ngắm được toàn cảnh bến cảng thật tuyệt.
items.explanation: Have a view of something is the fixed pattern for what you can see from a place. Sight is the ability to see or a place worth visiting, a scene is a part of a film or an event, and scenery is uncountable and never takes a.

items.q: ______ the film was three hours long, nobody left the cinema early.
items.vi: Mặc dù bộ phim dài ba tiếng, không ai rời rạp sớm cả.
items.explanation: A contrast introduced by a full clause (subject + verb) needs although. Despite must be followed by a noun or -ing form, however cannot join two clauses this way, and because gives a reason, which does not fit the meaning.

items.q: The picnic was cancelled because of the ______ rain on Sunday morning.
items.vi: Buổi dã ngoại bị hủy vì trận mưa lớn sáng Chủ nhật.
items.explanation: Rain, traffic and snow are described as heavy. Strong collocates with wind or coffee, and hard and big are not used with rain.

items.q: Dad finally ______ and said that nobody could use a phone at the dinner table.
options: put his cards on the table
items.vi: Cuối cùng bố cũng cương quyết ra lệnh rằng không ai được dùng điện thoại trong bữa tối.
items.explanation: Put your foot down means to be firm and refuse to allow something. Put your feet up is to relax, put your back into it is to work hard, and put your cards on the table is to be honest about your plans.

items.q: If my brother ______ so much noise every evening, I could finish my book in a week.
items.vi: Nếu em trai tôi không làm ồn như vậy mỗi tối thì tôi có thể đọc xong cuốn sách trong một tuần.
items.explanation: This is a second conditional about a present situation that is not true (every evening + could finish), so the if-clause takes the past simple: didn't make. The present and future forms belong to the first conditional, and hadn't made would refer to a finished past event.

items.q: Our ______ was a quiet village by the sea, but the bus dropped us in the wrong town.
items.vi: Điểm đến của chúng tôi là một ngôi làng yên tĩnh ven biển, nhưng xe buýt lại thả chúng tôi ở nhầm thị trấn.
items.explanation: The place you are travelling to is your destination. Direction is the way you go (north, left), distance is how far it is, and arrival is the act of getting there, not the place itself.

items.q: Neither my parents nor my little sister ______ horror films.
items.vi: Cả bố mẹ tôi lẫn em gái tôi đều không thích phim kinh dị.
items.explanation: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it: my little sister likes. Like, are liking and have liked would agree with the plural parents, and like is a state verb that is not used in continuous forms anyway.

items.q: My cousin has ______ the piano and practises every evening after dinner.
items.vi: Em họ tôi mới bắt đầu học đàn piano và luyện tập mỗi tối sau bữa ăn.
items.explanation: Take up means to start a new hobby or activity. Take over is to take control of something, take in is to understand or to give someone a home, and take off is to remove clothes or to leave the ground.

items.q: The chocolate cake ______ by my grandmother was the best thing at the party.
items.vi: Chiếc bánh sô-cô-la do bà tôi làm là món ngon nhất trong bữa tiệc.
items.explanation: A past participle shortens the relative clause which was made by my grandmother: the cake made by. Making would mean the cake did the making, and was made / had made would give the sentence two main verbs.

items.q: This time next week we ______ on the beach in Nha Trang with all our cousins.
items.vi: Giờ này tuần sau chúng tôi sẽ đang nằm trên bãi biển Nha Trang cùng tất cả anh chị em họ.
items.explanation: This time next week points to an action in progress at a future moment, which takes the future continuous: will be lying. The present simple, present perfect and past continuous do not describe a future moment.

items.q: On the first day in Hue, my family went ______ and took photos of every old palace.
items.vi: Ngày đầu tiên ở Huế, gia đình tôi đi tham quan và chụp ảnh mọi cung điện cổ.
items.explanation: Go sightseeing is the set expression for visiting the famous places of a town. Watching and viewing need an object (watching a film), and go looking needs for something.

items.q: My brother and I often cook dinner ______ when our parents work late.
items.vi: Anh em tôi thường tự nấu bữa tối khi bố mẹ đi làm về muộn.
items.explanation: My brother and I = we, so the reflexive pronoun is ourselves (meaning without help). Ourself does not exist in standard English, themselves refers to they, and each other would mean we cook one another, which makes no sense.

items.q: Could you ______ a photo of us in front of the cinema, please?
items.vi: Bạn chụp giúp bọn mình một tấm ảnh trước rạp chiếu phim được không?
items.explanation: In English you take a photo. Make and do are the usual learner mistakes, and catch is used with a bus, a ball or a cold, not a photo.

items.q: Let's watch a comedy tonight, ______?
items.vi: Tối nay chúng ta xem phim hài nhé?
items.explanation: A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?. Will you follows an imperative, and do / don't we follow a present simple statement with we.
